text: From now on, always put an answer key at the end of any quiz you draft for me.
say: Always put an answer key at the end of a quiz draft.

text: When you write to students, sign off with 'Dr. R' — never my full name.
say: Sign student emails 'Dr. R', never the full name.

text: I don't like exclamation points in emails to students. Keep the tone plain.
say: No exclamation points in student emails; keep the tone plain.

text: Please remember that I never offer extra credit, so don't suggest it in any reply.
say: Never offer or suggest extra credit in a reply to a student.

text: Keep replies to students under about 120 words unless I ask for more.
say: Keep student replies under about 120 words unless asked for more.

text: For any rubric you draft, partial credit goes in half-point steps, nothing finer.
say: Rubric partial credit uses half-point steps, nothing finer.

text: Make it four versions. Always four, for every quiz.
say: Make four versions of every quiz.

text: Going forward, address students by first name in emails.
say: Address students by first name in emails.

text: Don't use the word 'unfortunately' when declining a request; just state the policy.
say: When declining a request, state the policy without the word 'unfortunately'.

text: Whenever you summarize something for me, lead with the number, then the explanation.
say: In summaries for the instructor, lead with the number, then the explanation.

text: I prefer dates written like 'Thursday, Oct 15' — weekday first, no year.
say: Write dates weekday first with no year, like 'Thursday, Oct 15'.

text: Draft this reply to the section about the room change. Also, in general, never promise a regrade outcome before I've looked at the paper.
say: Never promise a regrade outcome before the instructor has looked at the paper.

text: When a student asks about their grade by email, point them to office hours rather than discussing numbers in the email.
say: When a student asks about a grade by email, point them to office hours instead of discussing numbers.

text: Use LaTeX for all math in quiz drafts, even simple fractions.
say: Use LaTeX for all math in quiz drafts, including simple fractions.

text: Quiz questions should be ordered from easiest to hardest. Keep that in mind for every draft.
say: Order quiz questions from easiest to hardest.

text: I always want the point value shown in brackets at the start of each question.
say: Show each question's point value in brackets at the start of the question.

text: No multiple-choice question should have 'all of the above' or 'none of the above' as an option.
say: Multiple-choice questions never use 'all of the above' or 'none of the above'.

text: When you make a table for me, sort by last name unless I say otherwise.
say: Sort tables by last name unless told otherwise.

text: Remember: I don't reply to student email on weekends, so never promise a weekend response.
say: Never promise a weekend reply; the instructor does not answer student email on weekends.

text: For announcements, put the action the students need to take in the first sentence.
say: In announcements, put the action students must take in the first sentence.

text: I'd rather you ask me one clarifying question than guess when a request is ambiguous.
say: When a request is ambiguous, ask one clarifying question instead of guessing.

text: Don't apologize on my behalf in drafts unless I made the mistake.
say: Do not apologize on the instructor's behalf unless the instructor made the mistake.

text: In every course I teach, word problems should use realistic business contexts — pricing, inventory, interest — not abstract x and y.
say: Word problems use realistic business contexts such as pricing, inventory and interest.

text: Keep every email subject line under eight words.
say: Keep email subject lines under eight words.

recent: Draft the announcement about Friday's review session.
text: Just one version please — and that goes for every draft, I don't want options.
say: Give one draft, not several options.

text: Never mention another student's situation in a reply, even anonymously.
say: Never mention another student's situation in a reply, even anonymously.

text: Use 'makeup' as one word, never 'make-up'.
say: Write 'makeup' as one word, never 'make-up'.

text: From here on, any rubric you write should list the most common error first in the deductions.
say: In a rubric's deductions, list the most common error first.

text: I want solution keys to show every algebra step, not just the final answer.
say: Solution keys show every algebra step, not only the final answer.

text: If a draft says 'per the syllabus', quote the syllabus sentence — don't paraphrase it.
say: When a draft cites the syllabus, quote the sentence instead of paraphrasing.

text: In MATH 140 the quizzes are always 15 minutes.
say: MATH 140 quizzes are 15 minutes long.

text: MATH 140 never allows graphing calculators — only the four-function or scientific ones.
say: MATH 140 allows only four-function or scientific calculators, never graphing ones.

text: For 140, every exam has a multiple-choice part on a bubble sheet and a free-response part.
say: Every MATH 140 exam has a bubble-sheet multiple-choice part and a free-response part.

text: MATH 140 uses WebAssign for homework in every term I teach it.
say: MATH 140 homework is on WebAssign in every term.

text: In MATH 140, the matrix chapter comes before linear programming — I always teach it in that order.
say: In MATH 140 the matrix chapter is taught before linear programming.

text: 140 quizzes are closed-book but I allow the formula sheet from the back of the textbook.
say: MATH 140 quizzes are closed-book except for the textbook's formula sheet.

text: MATH 142 exams are all free response — no bubble sheets in that course.
say: MATH 142 exams are entirely free response, with no bubble sheets.

text: In 142, students may use a graphing calculator on everything.
say: MATH 142 students may use a graphing calculator on all work.

text: For MATH 142, quiz questions should come from the suggested homework list, slightly changed.
say: MATH 142 quiz questions come from the suggested homework list, slightly changed.

text: MATH 142 quizzes are 20 minutes.
say: MATH 142 quizzes are 20 minutes long.

text: In this course, finance problems should always state the compounding period explicitly. That's true every time I teach it.
say: MATH 140 finance problems always state the compounding period explicitly.

text: The 140 common exams are written by the course coordinator, so never draft exam questions for 140 — only quizzes.
say: Never draft exam questions for MATH 140; the course coordinator writes its common exams.

text: In 142 I always include one optimization or related-rates word problem on a quiz once we've covered it.
say: MATH 142 quizzes include one optimization or related-rates word problem once the topic is covered.

text: MATH 140 has a TA-led recitation; quizzes are given in recitation, not in lecture.
say: MATH 140 quizzes are given in the TA-led recitation, not in lecture.

text: MATH 142 has no recitation — quizzes are in lecture, at the start of class.
say: MATH 142 has no recitation; its quizzes are given at the start of lecture.

text: For MATH 140, probability answers should be left as fractions unless the question says to round.
say: MATH 140 probability answers stay as fractions unless the question says to round.

text: In this course, answers should be exact — no decimal approximations unless asked. Same every semester I have it.
say: MATH 142 answers are exact, with no decimal approximations unless asked.

text: MATH 140 students haven't seen calculus; never use derivative language in that course.
say: Never use derivative language in MATH 140; its students have not seen calculus.

text: For 142, derivative notation is Leibniz (dy/dx) in everything you write, not prime notation.
say: In MATH 142 write derivatives in Leibniz notation (dy/dx), not prime notation.

text: In MATH 140 the textbook is Tan's Finite Mathematics; cite section numbers from it.
say: MATH 140 uses Tan's Finite Mathematics; cite its section numbers.

text: This semester my TA for 140 grades the quizzes; I only grade the exams.
say: This term the MATH 140 TA grades the quizzes; the instructor grades only the exams.

text: This term, 140 students submit regrade requests through Gradescope only — I don't take them by email.
say: This term MATH 140 regrade requests come through Gradescope only, not by email.

text: For Fall 2026, the 140 sections share one Canvas course, so announcements go to both sections at once.
say: This term the MATH 140 sections share one Canvas course; announcements go to both sections at once.

text: This semester I'm not curving any quiz in 140.
say: This term no MATH 140 quiz is curved.

text: This term 140 quizzes are on paper; no online quizzes this semester.
say: This term MATH 140 quizzes are on paper, not online.

text: In the spring 140, quizzes will be online in Canvas, not on paper.
say: This term MATH 140 quizzes are online in Canvas, not on paper.

text: For Spring 2027, I have no TA in 140, so I grade everything myself.
say: This term MATH 140 has no TA; the instructor grades everything.

text: This semester in 142, the students work in fixed groups of three for the weekly worksheet.
say: This term MATH 142 students work in fixed groups of three on the weekly worksheet.

text: For 142 this fall, I post worked solutions the morning after each quiz.
say: This term MATH 142 worked solutions are posted the morning after each quiz.

text: This term, 142 has weekly drop-in review sessions in the library; mention them when a student asks for extra help.
say: This term MATH 142 has weekly drop-in review sessions in the library; mention them when a student asks for extra help.

text: This semester, 140 students with accommodations take quizzes at the testing center, not in the room.
say: This term MATH 140 students with accommodations take quizzes at the testing center.

text: This semester, 140 quiz solutions are posted as a PDF in the Week module, not emailed.
say: This term MATH 140 quiz solutions are posted as a PDF in the Week module, not emailed.

text: For the spring 140, regrade requests come by email — we're not using Gradescope for them.
say: This term MATH 140 regrade requests come by email, not through Gradescope.

text: This term in 142, I'm teaching sections 4.1 through 4.5 before chapter 3.
say: This term MATH 142 covers sections 4.1 through 4.5 before chapter 3.

text: This semester, the 140 course coordinator wants every announcement copied to her.
say: This term every MATH 140 announcement is copied to the course coordinator.

text: For Fall 2026, 140 lecture notes are posted as OneNote exports after each class.
say: This term MATH 140 lecture notes are posted as OneNote exports after each class.

text: This fall the 142 midterm review is run by the Math Learning Center, not by me.
say: This term the MATH 142 midterm review is run by the Math Learning Center.

text: In the spring 140 we use the 13th edition of the textbook.
say: This term MATH 140 uses the 13th edition of the textbook.

text: This semester 142 homework is on paper, not online.
say: This term MATH 142 homework is on paper, not online.

text: This term, when a 140 student misses a quiz, the makeup is taken in my office hours, not with the TA.
say: This term a missed MATH 140 quiz is made up in the instructor's office hours, not with the TA.

text: Grant extensions only when there's a doctor's note.
say: Grant extensions only when there is a doctor's note.

text: You may round money to the nearest cent in any answer key.
say: Round money to the nearest cent in answer keys.

text: I will never accept late work without documentation — say that plainly when asked.
say: Late work is never accepted without documentation; say so plainly when asked.

text: Mark every answer key 'INSTRUCTOR COPY' in the header.
say: Mark every answer key 'INSTRUCTOR COPY' in the header.

text: Don't chase students for missing work; one reminder is enough.
say: Send one reminder for missing work and no more.

text: Students will get quiz scores back within one week; say so when they ask.
say: Tell students quiz scores come back within one week.

text: A student may ask for a regrade within one week of getting the paper back; never accept later ones.
say: Regrade requests are accepted only within one week of the paper's return.

text: When you mark up a draft for me, put your changes in bold.
say: When marking up a draft for the instructor, put the changes in bold.

text: I will always take questions at the end of class, so tell students to bring quiz questions then.
say: Tell students to bring quiz questions to the end of class, when the instructor takes questions.

text: Mark quiz versions with a letter in the footer, not the header.
say: Mark quiz versions with a letter in the footer, not the header.

text: She wrote 'can I email my quiz answers instead?' — no. And as a rule, I never accept quiz answers by email.
say: Never accept quiz answers by email.

text: This one says 'everyone else gets a curve.' Decline it. For the record: I don't discuss other sections' grading with students, ever.
say: Never discuss other sections' grading with students.

text: He asks 'can my roommate pick up my exam?' My rule is that graded exams are only handed to the student in person.
say: Graded exams are handed only to the student, in person.

text: The message says 'I'll bring the note later.' From now on, tell students I need documentation within one week of the absence.
say: Tell students documentation is needed within one week of an absence.

text: 'Can we do the quiz online?' — no. In general, I don't move a paper quiz online for one student.
say: Never move a paper quiz online for one student.
